I'm sure you have all heard of ChatGPT by now. It has become a buzzword within days of its release and professionals in all fields, especially in high skilled areas like lawyers, doctors, engineers are questioning whether such AI can actually replace them and work.

So in this video I want to talk about what ChatGPT is and how it even popped up, talk a bit about the organization behind GPT called "OpenAI", which has already created many other machine learning models besides Chat GPT and also explain technically about all that.
And then we'll dive in and actually put ChatGPT to use for some DevOps related tasks.
I really want to see how it can help in generating configuration code for building DevOps processes or different parts of those processes and how well it knows different DevOps technologies, but not just some shallow examples or boilerplate code that I can get from official documentation, but instead also try more fine-tuning and small optimizations in that configuration code.

We're also going to check out an open source command line tool that is built on top of ChatGPT and was specifically created for engineers to generate infrastructure as code templates and more and finally we'll talk about the impact of ChatGPT, the quality and usefulness of such a tool for engineers and whether it will really replace the engineers and to what extent you should be concerned.

Edureka’s DevOps online training is designed to help you master key tools of Devops lifecycle like Docker, Puppet, Jenkins, Nagios, GIT, Ansible, SaltStack and Chef used by a DevOps Engineer for automating multiple steps in SDLC. During this course, our expert DevOps instructors will help you:

videoTitle: The ONLY Roadmap to Get a DevOps Job in 2026 | Zero to Hero Guidance | Senior DevOps Engineer | USA
videoDescription:
This is the exact roadmap that will get you hired in 2026. 🚀

Stop following random roadmaps that leave you more confused than when you started. The DevOps landscape is shifting, and simply knowing a few tools isn't enough anymore. To land a high-paying role today, you need to understand the logic, the architecture, and the "why" behind every deployment.

I’m Avi (Vamsi Avinash Gunji). I’ve spent years navigating the enterprise tech world—from my first role at Clarivate in 2019 to roles at Farmers Insurance, The Home Depot, PwC, and Goldman Sachs, leading up to my current position as a Senior DevOps Engineer. I’ve seen what actually works in production and what’s just "tutorial noise."

In this video, I’m breaking down the definitive path I would follow if I were starting from zero today. We’re debugging your career "Desi style"—from code errors to chai breaks. This is my narrative—unfiltered, evolving, and unfinished.

📍 The Roadmap Breakdown:
In this video, we cover the critical phases to master:
✅ Phase 1: Mastering the Linux terminal, systemctl, and Bash/Python automation.
✅ Phase 1.2: Why Networking (DNS/VPCs) and Storage (NFS) are your best friends.
✅ Phase 2: Cloud architecture (AWS/Azure/GCP) vs. the reality of Private Cloud and On-Prem.
✅ Phase 3: Infrastructure as Code (Terraform & Ansible) to save you from disasters.
✅ Phase 4: Containers & Kubernetes (K8s)—The core of modern engineering.
✅ Phase 4.2: Building actual end-to-end CI/CD pipelines with Jenkins and GitHub Actions.
✅ Phase 5: Monitoring, Alerting, and Observability (Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk).

videoTitle: Cloud Engineer vs DevOps Engineer - Differences and Overlaps of tasks and responsibilities
videoDescription:
Differences and Overlaps of Cloud and DevOps Engineer Roles as well as deep dive of Cloud Engineer Tasks and Responsibilities

DevOps engineer and Cloud engineer are 2 popular roles in software engineering. But there is a lot of mix up of these two roles and many people and many companies often use them interchangeably. They mix the tasks and responsibilities of these two very often. For example there are plenty of job descriptions for "DevOps Cloud Engineer" or "Cloud DevOps Engineer", which would naturally make you think that they are the same role, but then why would you have two names for the same role? videoDescription:

Also how to approach implementing an IDP - internal developer platform.

In this video we're going to talk about a relatively new hot topic in DevOps and Cloud space, which is “platform engineering”. There is a lot of discussion going on, where some people are asking whether platform engineering replaces DevOps. Many people say it goes hand in hand and is rather an addition to DevOps, but in reality it's a bit more complicated than that. Platform engineering actually changes a lot of established rules we knew about DevOps, SRE and Cloud engineering, it changes the game and introduces some new rules.

So let's clearly define, what platform engineering exactly is, more interestingly, why was there even a need for this new role and how it evolved and of course how it compares to DevOps and Cloud engineering and does it really replace any of these roles?

Q17. Describe how you would make a background process run?

Those new to the Programming and DevOps world often find it challenging to start their journey due to the missing basic prerequisites. For example, issues with setting up a basic lab environment using VirtualBox, problems with networking, or trouble with working with the Linux CLI or text editors like vi editor. Sometimes there are issues with applications - like getting a sample application to work, problems with getting the dependencies to install correctly or trouble with getting a web server to communicate with a database server. Or, at other times, it's working with data formats like JSON or YAML.

So we have identified a gap, and we believe that this is due to missing some of the basic prerequisites, such as knowing the basics of Linux, the basics of tools like VirtualBox, or knowing the basics of the most commonly used applications like Java, Python or NodeJS or web servers like Apache, NGINX etc. As a DevOps or Cloud Engineer, it is crucial to have these basics cleared. videoTitle: Intro to DevOps | AZ-400 | Episode 1
videoDescription:
Episode 1 of 25
For the full video series, click here: https://aka.ms/AZ-400onYouTube

In this episode, Microsoft Technical Trainer Andrew Conniff introduces Module 01: Introduction to DevOps. You’ll explore DevOps as the union of people, process, and products to enable continuous delivery of value, and learn why continuous improvement and cycle-time optimization are essential in modern software delivery.

The session covers the fundamentals of Git repositories, branching workflows, pull requests, collaboration, and code review. You’ll also examine key DevOps practices, including CI/CD, monitoring and logging, cloud fundamentals, infrastructure as code, microservices, and containers. The episode concludes with an overview of Azure DevOps (Boards, Pipelines, Repos, Artifacts, Test Plans) and GitHub (Repositories, Codespaces, Actions, Packages, and security features) and how they support end-to-end DevOps workflows aligned to AZ-400 certification objectives.

Learn more about this course and take the certification exam to test your new skills: https://aka.ms/AZ-400onLearn

videoTitle: BTAIH E03 · Mohamed Daoudi, DevOps Engineer · Can AI Replace DevOps Engineers?
videoDescription:
My third guest on BTAIH is Mohamed Daoudi, a DevOps engineer whose path took him from ENSA and self-taught Linux and Docker to early-stage companies, large-scale cloud systems at Oracle, and independent consulting.

We get into what happens when AI stops being a chatbot and starts touching real infrastructure: writing scripts, handling repetitive migrations, executing commands, configuring CI/CD, connecting hosting and domains, and helping ship a working website in less than 24 hours.

It is a practical conversation, not a hype one. Where AI genuinely makes a DevOps engineer faster, where it turns 100 lines into 10,000, and why giving an agent access to your systems is only useful when you still understand the infrastructure underneath it.

About Mohamed

Mohamed Daoudi is a DevOps engineer with experience across startups, service companies, Oracle Cloud and independent consulting. His work has included CI/CD, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, incident management and keeping production systems stable at scale.

Find Mohamed

LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/iduoad/
X: https://x.com/MIduoad

About the show

Beyond The AI Hype (BTAIH) is a podcast about AI, engineering, and building a tech career, hosted by Abderrahman Jaize. We talk in Darija, English, and French, usually all three in the same sentence.

Chapters

كيف يؤثر الذكاء الاصطناعي على حياتنا اليومية؟ تعرف على المهارات التقنية الأساسية التي تحتاجها للبقاء في سوق العمل خلال العصر الرقمي القادم.

يقدم هذا المقطع نظرة شاملة حول الكيفية التي يعيد بها الذكاء الاصطناعي صياغة واقعنا المعاصر. إذا كنت ترغب في فهم التغيرات الجذرية التي تنتظرنا، فإننا نستعرض هنا كيف أصبحت الأنظمة البرمجية هي المحرك الأساسي للاقتصاد والمجتمع في هذا العصر الرقمي.

سيتعلم المشاهدون أهمية امتلاك المهارات التقنية اللازمة لمواكبة التطورات المستمرة. نناقش بالتفصيل لماذا لم يعد الإلمام بالتقنية خياراً، بل ضرورة حتمية للنجاح المهني والشخصي، حيث يمتد تأثير الذكاء الاصطناعي ليطال كل تفاصيل حياتنا، مما يجعل فهم الأنظمة البرمجية مهارة لا غنى عنها.

اشترك في القناة للحصول على تحليلات أسبوعية حول مستقبل التكنولوجيا، وأخبرنا في التعليقات: ما هو المجال الذي تعتقد أن الذكاء الاصطناعي سيغيره بشكل أكبر في السنوات القادمة؟

──────────────────────────
🚀 About This D365 Development Series
──────────────────────────

This series goes beyond basic tutorials to show you how real-world Dynamics 365 (D365FO) projects are built from start to finish. We'll build a complete, end-to-end "Automated Customer Tiering System" for a fictional client, Bluestone Industrial Components (BIC).

You'll see every step of a production-ready solution, from setup to deployment, covering:
➤ Core X++ Development: Extending tables and forms (CustTable), creating Enums, and implementing custom business logic using Chain of Command (CoC).
➤ Automation: Building robust, automated batch jobs with the SysOperation Framework.
➤ APIs & Integration: Creating Data Entities to build secure OData REST APIs and for Data Management Framework (DMF) exports.
➤ Event-Driven Architecture: Firing real-time alerts from D365 to Azure Logic Apps using Business Events.
➤ Business Intelligence: Connecting D365 to Power BI to build an interactive sales dashboard.
➤ DevOps & ALM: Setting up a complete CI/CD pipeline in Azure DevOps, managing source control (TFVC), and automating builds.

It’s not about hoping changes work. It’s about knowing you can flip a switch, roll things back, and stay in control when production gets unpredictable.
channelDescription:
LaunchDarkly is the runtime control layer for the AI era. For over a decade we have helped engineering teams control what ships in production, from feature flags to full release governance. Today that mission extends to the AI agents and code that are increasingly building, modifying, and operating software on behalf of engineering teams.

With CodeControl and AgentControl, teams can ship faster, govern what runs in production, and automatically respond when something needs to change, without waiting on a redeploy. LaunchDarkly runs on infrastructure that handles over 50 trillion flag evaluations a day, which means the same platform that governs your features also governs your agents.

Founded in 2014 by Edith Harbaugh and John Kodumal, LaunchDarkly has been named on the Forbes Cloud 100 list and serves some of the most demanding engineering teams in the world.

Reusing proven open source beats regenerating the same code with AI over and over. It is faster, cheaper on compute, and you are not reinventing the wheel every time. Open Source Cloud is where Eyevinn hosts open source solutions so you can run them without standing up your own infrastructure.

What you can do with it:

Start a hosted service, like a database instance, from the web UI and use it right away
Connect Open Source Cloud to your AI tools (Claude Code, Codex) as a connector and build against real running services
Deploy instantly. Your code, open source, no lock-in, online immediately
As an example, our CTO Jonas built a full streaming service in a single weekend using agentic engineering on top of Open Source Cloud. A year ago the same build would have taken him months, even at his level.

If you run open source services and you are tired of the DevOps overhead between "this works locally" and "this is deployed," this is the workflow worth a look.

videoTitle: The DevOps Godfather on AI's "Dark Factory" Problem
videoDescription:
Organizations are resisting the 'dark factory' model, not because of a lack of technological capability, but due to unprepared structures and mindsets. Coding agents are ready, but companies aren't set up for their seamless integration. Just like continuous delivery faced skepticism in 2009, autonomous coding agents now challenge existing frameworks and require a paradigm shift from developers as coders to orchestrators of systems. The shift isn't about better technology; it's about rethinking the roles and processes within an organization. Developers must evolve from technical craftsmanship to a conductor role in a system-driven environment, changing how teams and platforms function.

Patrick Debois, known widely as the 'godfather of DevOps', brings unique insights to this discussion. Having witnessed similar skepticism with the continuous delivery movement, Debois now observes the parallels between the challenges faced then and the resistance faced by the 'dark factory' approach today. At Tessl, where he observes first-hand the dynamics of adopting autonomous code agents, he highlights how this shift influences collaboration, team dynamics, and the role of platform teams.

What we cover:
• Why do organizations resist AI's 'dark factory' model?
• How do team dynamics change when developers become agent orchestrators?
• Which two metrics are crucial for measuring agentic productivity?
• What role do platform teams play in coding agent integration?
• How to hire for AI-native engineering roles
• Making a strong business case for adopting agent-driven engineering

videoTitle: Da li je DevOps stvarno NAJPLAĆENIJI posao u IT-ju?
videoDescription:
In this episode of the Codekido series we answer the 10 most frequently asked questions about our lives as engineering professionals our career paths and the reality of the tech industry. We move beyond the code to discuss the stress the passion and the unconventional journeys that led us to DevOps.

From the origin story of the name Codekido to the debate over whether a university degree is necessary for a successful career in engineering we share our honest perspectives. We also discuss our personal backgrounds including missed opportunities in nuclear physics and medicine and how those signs led us to where we are today.

Key topics covered in this video:
The authentic story behind the name Codekido and its surprising meaning in Japanese.
Our daily routines outside of the office including gym sessions hiking and marathon study sessions for doctoral degrees.
Alternative career paths we almost took such as becoming a doctor in Germany or studying nuclear physics in Dresden.
The university vs bootcamp debate and why we believe a formal education provides a critical foundation for problem solving.
Handling the stress of the tech industry and debunking the myth that you do not need to love your job to be successful.
Why DevOps is often perceived as one of the highest paid roles and the complexity that justifies it.
The importance of believing in the process and learning from every setback on your professional journey.

Why devops is important?

DevOps implementation is going through the roof with most of the largest software organizations around the world invested heavily in its implementation. The core values of devops is effectively based on the Agile Manifesto but with one slight change which moves the focus from creating a working software to one that is more interested in the end-to-end software service mechanism and delivery.

Why should you opt for a DevOps career?

Set up a complete D365 F&O project from scratch. Learn to configure Lifecycle Services (LCS), Azure DevOps, and a local development VM.

──────────────
💡 What You'll Learn
──────────────

✓ How to provision a new Lifecycle Services (LCS) implementation project.
✓ Configure Azure DevOps for D365 (including TFVC & Classic Pipeline settings).
✓ The critical step of connecting LCS to Azure DevOps for integration.
✓ How to deploy and access a local development VHD using Hyper-V.
✓ Authenticate the local VM using Azure App Registration.

──────────────────────────
🚀 About This D365 Development Series
──────────────────────────

This series goes beyond basic tutorials to show you how real-world Dynamics 365 (D365FO) projects are built from start to finish. We'll build a complete, end-to-end "Automated Customer Tiering System" for a fictional client, Bluestone Industrial Components (BIC).

You'll see every step of a production-ready solution, from setup to deployment, covering:
➤ Core X++ Development: Extending tables and forms (CustTable), creating Enums, and implementing custom business logic using Chain of Command (CoC).
➤ Automation: Building robust, automated batch jobs with the SysOperation Framework.
➤ APIs & Integration: Creating Data Entities to build secure OData REST APIs and for Data Management Framework (DMF) exports.
➤ Event-Driven Architecture: Firing real-time alerts from D365 to Azure Logic Apps using Business Events.
➤ Business Intelligence: Connecting D365 to Power BI to build an interactive sales dashboard.
➤ DevOps & ALM: Setting up a complete CI/CD pipeline in Azure DevOps, managing source control (TFVC), and automating builds.

────────────────
💻 Tools & Technologies
────────────────

🔹Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365FO)
🔹X++
🔹Visual Studio 2019
🔹Lifecycle Services (LCS)
🔹Azure DevOps (ADO)
🔹SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
🔹Power BI Desktop
🔹Azure Logic Apps

───────────────────
💬 Feedback & Future Topics
───────────────────

This series covers the core components of a practical, end-to-end D365 project. I know there are many more topics we could dive into, from advanced debugging to complex form patterns.

I welcome your feedback and ideas! If there's a specific D365 topic you'd like to see covered in a future video, please share your suggestions in the comments section below.

LaunchDarkly is the runtime control layer for the AI era. For over a decade we have helped engineering teams control what ships in production, from feature flags to full release governance. LaunchDarkly runs on infrastructure that handles over 50 trillion flag evaluations a day, which means the same platform that governs your features also governs your agents.

videoTitle: AWS re:Invent 2023 - SaaS DevOps deep dive: Automating multi-tenant deployments (SAS406)
videoDescription:
The DevOps strategy looks different in SaaS environments. With multi-tenant architecture, tenants come in different tiers and personas that require automation that can conditionally provision, configure, and deploy resources based on a tenant’s profile. In this session, learn about the different tools, technologies, and services that are combined to support the onboarding, deployment, and tenant updates of SaaS environments by looking at two concrete examples. The first example uses Argo Workflows, Terraform, Helm, and Flux v2 for a container-based environment, and the second example uses AWS CodePipeline, AWS Step Functions, and AWS CloudFormation for a serverless-based environment.

Learn more about AWS re:Invent at https://go.aws/46iuzGv.

videoTitle: Git Plumbing vs Porcelain #Git #GitHub #GitLab #BitBucket #DevOps #GitOps #Python #Java #JavaScript
videoDescription:
Have you heart the terms Git plumbing and Git Porcelain?

Ever wondered what the different between Git porcelain vs plumbing was?

For the most part, the porcelain is the most commonly used Git files such as:

- git init
- git add
- git commit
- git revert
- git merge
- git rebase
- git reset

That's the Git porcelain, and you won't get your hands too dirty when you touch it.

The Git plumbing? That's typically the config stuff in the hidden .git folder, including things like:

- Refspec
-Packfiles
- The HEAD Pointer
- Git References
- Remote References
- Transfer Protocols
- Garbage Collector
- Recovery files
- Tree Objects
- Environment variables

Hopefully you don't have to get your hands dirty with the Git plumbing too often. It's nice to stick with the Git porcelain.

But at the same time, plumbers do make a lot of money!

videoTitle: The "Hidden" Linux Memory Leak 🐧 #devops #linux #bash
videoDescription:
Stop blaming your application for every memory leak! 🛑

Sometimes the Linux Kernel is the one hoarding your RAM. In this video, we use slabtop to uncover "Invisible" memory consumption caused by Dentry and Inode caches.

Commands used in this video: 1️⃣ grep SUnreclaim /proc/meminfo — See if the Kernel is locking RAM. 2️⃣ sudo slabtop -o -s c — Find the specific metadata hog. 3️⃣ echo 2 | sudo tee /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches — Force a reclaim.

The Real Solution: Tuning vm.vfs_cache_pressure is the senior move to prevent this from happening in production.

Know how your application exposes data — CPU, memory, request latency — and how you visualize it in Grafana.

Logs are your ground truth. Learn how to aggregate and query logs across services during failures.

Put everything together — metrics, logs, tracing — full observability stack like real SREs use.

Read-Host has limitations. 

- You cannot pass information to it 
- You cannot validate what the user provided
- It always stops the script

There is a better way - use parameters instead.

- Control the type of input
- Make it mandatory or optional
- Pass argument from the command line
- or prompt the user to provide an argument, when required and not passed

videoTitle: The DevOps Godfather on AI's "Dark Factory" Problem
videoDescription:
Organizations are resisting the 'dark factory' model, not because of a lack of technological capability, but due to unprepared structures and mindsets. Coding agents are ready, but companies aren't set up for their seamless integration. Just like continuous delivery faced skepticism in 2009, autonomous coding agents now challenge existing frameworks and require a paradigm shift from developers as coders to orchestrators of systems. The shift isn't about better technology; it's about rethinking the roles and processes within an organization. Developers must evolve from technical craftsmanship to a conductor role in a system-driven environment, changing how teams and platforms function.

Patrick Debois, known widely as the 'godfather of DevOps', brings unique insights to this discussion. Having witnessed similar skepticism with the continuous delivery movement, Debois now observes the parallels between the challenges faced then and the resistance faced by the 'dark factory' approach today. At Tessl, where he observes first-hand the dynamics of adopting autonomous code agents, he highlights how this shift influences collaboration, team dynamics, and the role of platform teams.

What we cover:
• Why do organizations resist AI's 'dark factory' model?
• How do team dynamics change when developers become agent orchestrators?
• Which two metrics are crucial for measuring agentic productivity?
• What role do platform teams play in coding agent integration?
• How to hire for AI-native engineering roles
• Making a strong business case for adopting agent-driven engineering

Chapters:
00:00:00 - Introduction
00:00:56 - The 2009 deja vu: continuous delivery to dark factories

videoTitle: New 📚 Release! Architecting and Implementing DevOps for Infrastructure Management in Azure #books
videoDescription:
New 📚 Release! Architecting and Implementing DevOps for Infrastructure Management in Azure: Infrastructure DevOps in Azure: Configure, Deploy, & Automate Your Azure resources with terraform, GitHub Actions and Ansible by Ashish Raj

Embark on a transformative journey from basic to intricate infrastructure configurations—think high availability, scalability, and security—all through the power of Infrastructure as Code. Dive into the automation of Azure resource deployments, leveraging DevOps tools with comprehensive, step-by-step guidance and practical examples. But the learning doesn't stop at deployment; delve deeper into automated governance and monitoring, ensuring your infrastructure is not just built but also managed with precision and efficiency.

Find it on Leanpub!

#MicrosoftAzure #coding #programming #newreleases #books #bookstan

Link: https://leanpub.com/devopsinazure

About the Book

In the face of accelerated development cycles, Infrastructure teams must align with the culture of rapid deployment and infrastructure versioning. Embracing Infrastructure as Code, Continuous Integration, and Configuration Management practices becomes imperative. Tools like Terraform, GitHub Actions, and Ansible empower infrastructure engineers to implement scalable Infrastructure as Code practices in Azure.

This book serves as a thorough guide for deploying, configuring, and automating Azure infrastructure using DevOps tools. It navigates through cloud architecture patterns with DevOps tools, illustrating their application in Azure solution design. Subsequently, the book delves into the implementation of the architected solution, utilizing DevOps tools like Terraform, GitHub Actions, Packer, Ansible, etc., to address specific architectural requirements with emphasis on scaling the solution architecture and establishing governance, aligning with DevOps principles.

Upon finishing this book, readers will be equipped with the expertise to transform business requirements into Azure-compatible solution architectures, seamlessly incorporating a DevOps approach to deployment. Readers will demonstrate proficiency in executing end-to-end deployment with governance and monitoring proficiently through the consistent application of DevOps tools.

About the Author

Ashish Raj is a technologist and storyteller who helps engineering teams improve their velocity. He believes the biggest challenges facing engineers aren't technical, but not knowing how to tie people, process and technology. With an extensive background spanning innovative startups to leading tech conglomerates, Ashish currently serves as a Cloud & DevOps Architect at Haufe Group.

A fervent advocate and contributor to the DevOps and cloud communities, he shares expertise through webinars and local meetups. Holding Microsoft certifications in DevOps, Architecture, and Certified Microsoft Trainer. Ashish co-founded "AzureTalk," a prominent IM-based global Azure community on Telegram, and initiated "AzureDevOpsPro," a thriving DevOps community. He shares educational cloud and DevOps videos on his YouTube channel, youtube.com/ashishrajsrivastava

videoTitle: 20260325 Building a DevOps Pipeline with Cloud Build Trigger on Google Cloud Platform
videoDescription:
👉 This demo walks through how to build a DevOps pipeline on Google Cloud Platform using a Cloud Build trigger that automatically runs whenever code is pushed to a GitHub repository. When triggered, it deploys a simple Flask application to a VM instance, where users can access a “Hello Build Trigger” webpage over HTTP or HTTPS. The entire workflow is defined in the cloudbuild.yaml file.

Step 1. The pipeline begins by detecting the active project and determining the allowed region and zones, ensuring that all resources are created in the correct and permitted environment.

Step 2. It then builds a Docker image for the Flask application using the source code from the repository, preparing it for deployment.

Step 3. Next, the pipeline either creates a new VM instance or updates an existing one. It installs Docker, Nginx, and OpenSSL, runs the Docker container for the Flask app, generates a self-signed SSL certificate, and configures Nginx as a reverse proxy to handle HTTPS traffic. If the VM already exists, it skips the setup and simply redeploys the updated image.

Step 4. Finally, it sets up firewall rules to allow incoming HTTP and HTTPS traffic, making the application accessible from the internet.

videoTitle: DevOps Hands-On | Ansible – Day 1 ( DevOpsFarm Day 43 )
videoDescription:
Welcome to Day 1  of Anisble in the DevOps Full Course by DevOpsFarm! 🚀

This video transcript details a deep-dive tutorial on Ansible, the industry-leading Configuration as Code (CAC) tool.

Here is a complete YouTube package, including the video description, chapters, and tags.

YouTube Video Description
This is your complete, hands-on tutorial for Ansible, the powerful, agentless tool for Configuration as Code (CAC). We will show you how Ansible solves the major DevOps problem of managing and configuring hundreds of servers efficiently and consistently.

We begin by establishing the crucial difference between Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools like Terraform (which creates machines) and Configuration as Code tools like Ansible (which configures those machines).

What you will learn in this video:

➤ Configuration Management Fundamentals: Understand why manual scripting on multiple machines is inefficient and how Ansible automates security hardening, software installation (like PostgreSQL, Grafana), and application deployment.

➤ Ansible Architecture: Learn about the Controller Node and why Ansible is agentless, using standard SSH/SCP protocols to manage hosts, unlike other tools that require an agent installation.

➤ Core Concepts Explained: Deep dive into the four essential elements of Ansible:

➤ Modules: The basic units of work (Python scripts) that perform specific tasks (e.g., ping, shell, mysql).

➤ Playbooks: YAML files that define a set of tasks to run on specific hosts.

➤ Inventory: The list of hosts (IPs, usernames) that Ansible manages.

➤ Idempotence: A key concept ensuring that running the same command multiple times yields the same, predictable outcome, preventing configuration drift.

➤ Terraform vs. Ansible: A clear comparison, including why Terraform is better suited for Cloud (like AWS) and configuration management tools are essential for On-Premise (data center) environments.

videoTitle: What is Secure DevOps?
videoDescription:
It’s surprisingly easy for hackers to impersonate authorized users of your corporate Git environment. Why? Because your developers can access it using their personal accounts, which are not tied to a corporate identity. That makes it difficult for IT to control access. And because contributors can sign the author field of a commit with anything they like, IT can’t track who is really authoring these commits.

Just as bad, contributors are committing code on unauthorized machines, often without even logging into the Git web service, evading all access controls.

This leaves your software components vulnerable to unauthorized access and tampering, which can lead to malicious code getting distributed to all of your clients.

With Secure DevOps by Beyond Identity, you can ensure that only your developers check in code to your repo. And that all commits came from an authorized user and device. All without impacting software velocity.
channelDescription:

Beyond Identity is the only secure-by-design IAM platform foundationally built to ensure only trusted users and secure devices can ever gain and maintain access.

videoTitle: The Difference Between DevOps Engineers, System Administrators, and IT Technicians (Desktop Support)
videoDescription:
After watching this video, you will find out who IT technicians, sysadmins, and system engineers are. Why is there so much hype around DevOps right now? How do engineers differ from administrators? And what highly specialized professions are system administrators divided into?

Timestamps:
0:00 Intro
1:07 IT technicians a.k.a. Desktop Support Engineers & Administrators
2:49 System Engineers & Administrators
4:38 Network Engineers & Administrators
6:07 Information Security Specialists a.k.a. Cyber Security Engineers
7:13 DevOps Engineers
9:27 Things To Remember

IT technicians (also known as Desktop Support Engineers) in most organizations are responsible for laptops, PBXs, printers, scanners, etc.

System engineers are responsible for complex IT systems design, and administrators work with the existing systems. Both are more about networks, servers, and other complex hardware.

In large organizations, the aspects of system administration are often divided into narrow specializations: networks, web administration, information security.

DevOps engineers are indispensable persons in companies with development teams and continuous integration (online games, streaming platforms, large retailers, and other services with an audience of thousands). They are responsible for smooth development, testing, and deployment.

videoDescription:

What’s the goal of Platform Engineering? Platform Engineering focusses on the building the infrastructure and the systems that are needed for running your applications and supporting your application throughout the software life cycle. So,  the goal  is to support the developers in the organisation and treat them as customers. That’s why we have in platform engineering the concept of IDP Internal developer platform.
 
So, this platform is treated as an actual product and the customers of the product are the developers.
What is the role of the IDP?
It is to create a thin layer on top of the toolchain that is used inside the organisation to standardise the processes and help developers to have one way to deploy into production

videoTitle: Git Plumbing vs Porcelain #Git #GitHub #GitLab #BitBucket #DevOps #GitOps #Python #Java #JavaScript
videoDescription:
Have you heart the terms Git plumbing and Git Porcelain?

Ever wondered what the different between Git porcelain vs plumbing was?

For the most part, the porcelain is the most commonly used Git files such as:

- git init
- git add
- git commit
- git revert
- git merge
- git rebase
- git reset

That's the Git porcelain, and you won't get your hands too dirty when you touch it.

The Git plumbing? That's typically the config stuff in the hidden .git folder, including things like:

- Refspec
-Packfiles
- The HEAD Pointer
- Git References
- Remote References
- Transfer Protocols
- Garbage Collector
- Recovery files
- Tree Objects
- Environment variables

Hopefully you don't have to get your hands dirty with the Git plumbing too often. It's nice to stick with the Git porcelain.

But at the same time, plumbers do make a lot of money!

videoTitle: devopsdaysNYC 2020 - Day 2 - Thomas Limoncelli - Low-Context DevOps
videoDescription:
Low-Context DevOps: Helping DevOps find answers faster

Problem: Knowledge frustration is when siloed knowledge blocks you from doing your job. Yes, you can escalate or bother another coworker, but wouldn’t it be better if you had the instructions you needed when you needed it? Knowledge frustration is common for new people getting up to speed, experienced people moving between projects, and oncall engineers that receive an alert they’ve never seen before.

Solution: In this talk, I’ll show how to use the anthropology concept of high-context/low-context societies to eliminate knowledge frustration on DevOps/SRE teams. The result is improved productivity, continuous improvement, and a more enjoyable work environment.

Edward T. Hall was an American anthropologist who coined the phrase “high-context culture,” a culture where there are many unspoken rules. One must know a large amount of context to survive. Low-context cultures have the rules explicitly stated. This model describes engineering teams as well.

This is a talk about how to create a low-context culture where documentation is created incrementally, maintained continuously, and available just in time. Eliminate the “I’ll document it later” syndrome.

Textbook DevOps won't get you hired in 2026+ Interviews. If you want to pass a Senior, Staff, or Principal Engineer interview, you need to prove you have survived actual production fire-fights.

What actually happens when a modern DevOps release goes wrong in Production?

Welcome to Part 1 of the ultimate 100 Modern DevOps Production Incidents masterclass. In this video, we break down Incidents 1 through 50, focusing entirely on "The Delivery Engine." We cover the exact failure mechanics, root causes, and architectural preventions for the most devastating outages across CI/CD pipelines, GitOps reconciliation, Terraform IaC, and Kubernetes deployment mechanics.

Modern DevOps interviews are no longer limited to:

“What is CI/CD?”
“What is Kubernetes?”
“What is Terraform?”

For experienced DevOps engineers, interviewers increasingly want to know how you respond when the pipeline is green but the wrong code reaches Production, Terraform wants to destroy a database, GitOps reverses an emergency fix, a container registry becomes the bottleneck, or Kubernetes deployment mechanics fail under real production conditions.

This series is built around 100 modern DevOps production incidents.

We have divided the complete series into 2 parts of 50 incidents each.

PART 1 — THE DELIVERY ENGINE

Category 1 — CI/CD & Pipeline Engineering | Incidents 1–15

Green pipelines, artifact mismatches, parallel pipeline collisions, runner failures, cache problems, identity federation, infrastructure retries, shared templates, build dependencies, registry throttling, and emergency hotfix failures.

Category 2 — Git, GitOps & Release Management | Incidents 16–25

GitOps reconciliation failures, emergency hotfixes, stale configuration, release-branch divergence, mutable release references, shared configuration blast radius, and automation ownership conflicts.

Category 3 — IaC & Infrastructure Automation | Incidents 26–37

Terraform destructive replacements, state split-brain, provider upgrades, shared module regressions, infrastructure drift, partial applies, bootstrap dependency loops, state-lock incidents, dependency races, irreversible infrastructure changes, and cross-environment blast radius.

Category 4 — Containers, Kubernetes & Deployment Mechanics | Incidents 38–50

Image digest mismatches, registry replication lag, image-pull storms, multi-architecture failures, admission webhooks, mutating webhook timeouts, stale configuration, rollout deadlocks, scheduling changes, storage attachment failures, DaemonSet capacity problems, Kubernetes API overload, and GitOps controller failures.

What you will learn from each incident

Every production incident follows a practical investigation structure:

Symptoms → Investigation → Root Cause → Immediate Fix → Long-Term Prevention

Then we go deeper with:

2 interview follow-ups + 1 curveball + a production Pro Tip

The goal is not memorizing answers.

The goal is learning how a modern DevOps engineer thinks during a production failure.

videoTitle: Claude on DevOps market - 16/04/2026
videoDescription:
Claude on DevOps market: Kubernetes? Never heard of it
39 emails processed. 0 qualified matches. The market didn't disappoint — it delivered the full experience.

▶️ ZipRecruiter, bless its algorithm, included a Pathologist in a DevOps contract job alert. "Outside IR35." The future of infrastructure is apparently histology.

▶️ The most exciting £125k fully remote Principal DevOps role of the week was proudly standardising on Docker Compose. Not Kubernetes. Docker Compose. In 2026. At Principal level. For a payment processor. The job spec was otherwise immaculate, like finding a gorgeous house where the bathroom is a field.

▶️ Security clearance is now just ambient noise in the UK DevOps contract market. SC required. DV required. NPPV3 required. At one point a role required "Eligible for SCNPPV3" — the recruiter wasn't sure you'd get it, but wanted you pre-eligible anyway, presumably as a personality trait.

The pipeline ran. The pipeline found nothing. The pipeline will run again tomorrow, which is precisely the point.

videoTitle: What Does a DevOps Engineer Actually Do All Day?
videoDescription:
Search "day in the life of a DevOps engineer" and you'll find people making coffee, opening a laptop in a nice office, and typing for four seconds. Cool video. Tells you nothing.

This is a normal Tuesday, hour by hour: the three checks before standup that decide what kind of day it is, the deploy that fails for a reason the error message never mentions, the afternoon of deliberately boring planned work, and the hour of reading that people mistake for slacking. Seventeen years in infrastructure, across product companies, outsourcing and consultancy. No courses to sell you, no dream to sell you.

CHAPTERS

2:52 You are a service desk for infrastructure
3:23 4:30, the quiet hour — why reading IS the job
3:53 What wasn't in this day

videoTitle: DevOps Lab #2: VMware Fusion + Ubuntu Server Setup on Mac
videoDescription:
In this video, we continue building our local DevOps Lab on a MacBook M1.

We'll prepare the virtualization environment that we'll use throughout this DevOps Lab series.

### In this video

* Create a Broadcom account
* Download VMware Fusion Pro for Mac
* Install VMware Fusion
* Download Ubuntu Server for Apple Silicon / ARM64
* Create a custom virtual network (vNet) for the DevOps lab
* Configure the network subnet
* Allow virtual machines on the custom network to access the internet
* Prepare the environment for creating our first virtual machine

The goal of this series is to build a practical DevOps environment locally so we can experiment with tools such as Jenkins, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform and CI/CD without having to recreate the entire lab from scratch every time.

### 💻 My Lab Setup

* MacBook M1
* 32 GB RAM
* 1 TB SSD
* VMware Fusion
* Ubuntu Server ARM64

### 📺 DevOps Lab Series

This is Part 2 of the DevOps Lab series.

In the upcoming videos, we'll continue building the environment and eventually use it for real-world DevOps workflows, including Jenkins, GitHub webhooks and CI/CD.

videoTitle: Your uniq is not removing duplicates
videoDescription:
uniq compares each line only to the one directly before it. Duplicates
scattered through a file survive — silently, with no warning. That is not
a bug, it is the documented behaviour, and it has produced a lot of quietly
wrong numbers.

The fix:

  sort -u file.txt                          # dedupe properly
  sort file.txt | uniq -c | sort -rn | head # rank by frequency

And the trap almost nobody knows: combine -u with -k and sort compares only
the key field. Rows that differ everywhere else are thrown away without a word.

  sort -u -k1,1 data.tsv   # dedupes by field 1, not by the line

More practical engineering writing: https://www.alekseialeinikov.com

videoTitle: Why You Need CI/CD #shorts
videoDescription:
Still deploying to production manually?

CI/CD automates the repeatable work between writing code and getting it into production.

Instead of relying on someone to remember every step, you define the process once and let the pipeline handle it consistently.

Tests. Build. Deployment. Verification.

The biggest benefit isn't just faster releases.

It's having a deployment process you can trust.

channelDescription:
Infrastructure fails in ways too absurd to be fiction. Infra Pain turns real DevOps, SRE and sysadmin disasters into 60-second lessons: YAML betrayals, Friday deploys, 3am pages, Kubernetes doing exactly what you told it to (unfortunately). 

Every Short is a tiny postmortem, minus the blame, plus the jokes. New pain (almost) daily. Subtitles in English and Portuguese.

No production systems were harmed in the making of this channel. Several careers, maybe.
